options.label: Grade 1: Asymptomatic or mild headache, slight nuchal rigidity
Grade 2: Moderate-severe headache, nuchal rigidity, no deficit except cranial nerve palsy
Grade 3: Drowsiness, confusion, or mild focal deficit
Grade 4: Stupor, moderate-severe hemiparesis, early decerebrate rigidity
Grade 5: Deep coma, decerebrate rigidity, moribund appearance

interpretation.label: Subarachnoid haemorrhage grading
interpretation.action: Higher grade is associated with worse prognosis and guides timing of aneurysm intervention.
